payload.headline: Tesla flat at 384.68 as a SpaceX merger is reported; still avoid

summary.thesis: Sales have stalled and margins and cash flow are shrinking, while the price sits near the top of Tesla's own valuation history, so the reported SpaceX merger talk changes the story but not the numbers.
summary.decision: Long-term avoid; swing wait until the price leaves the 363.93–404.4 band.
summary.act_at: Re-examine near 293.94; swing only on a close above 404.4 or a hold of 363.93–368.69

payload.happening: Tesla closed at 384.68, down 0.2%. That holds most of yesterday's jump and sits inside the 380.15–389.95 zone, just under resistance at 393.63–404.4. The Financial Times reported that directors are negotiating a SpaceX-Tesla merger, called the biggest ever. No filing confirms it. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: The merger report is about governance and sentiment, not about how many cars Tesla sells or what it earns on each one. Until terms are filed, it changes nothing in the reported numbers. SpaceX is a private rocket and satellite company with the same CEO (general knowledge), so a deal would raise questions about who gets what price and whether outside shareholders are treated fairly (general knowledge). The business picture itself is weak. Sales in the latest quarter fell 0.17% from a year earlier, after growing 15.78% two quarters ago. Operating margin slipped to 3.35% from 4.74%. Trailing free cash flow fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. Inventory rose 15% while sales were flat, and unsold cars can lead to price cuts. Each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, down from 33¢ three years ago. The balance sheet is not at risk: 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity mean the company can fund itself. What is at risk is profit: margins and cash generation are going the wrong way.

worth.text: At 384.68, Tesla is worth about 1521.0B. That is 423.3 times trailing earnings and 14.7 times sales. Its price-to-sales ratio is higher than 77.0% of its own last five years. A cash-flow model (DCF) built on the 3.3B of free cash flow gives 20.01 to 44.3 per share, with a base of 24.66. Even if sales started growing 30% a year, that model gives only 45.31. Comparing the price with Tesla's own price-to-sales history gives 203.8 at the low end, 293.94 in the middle and 399.81 at the top. The gap between the two methods comes from one assumption: whether you value Tesla on the cash it makes today or on the high multiple the market has paid for its future before. The filings note that the price needs about 50% a year growth, while Tesla has delivered 3% a year over three years. I use the own-history range, because the DCF ignores what the market has actually paid for this stock. Even so, the price is above the middle of that range.
worth.key_assumption: With flat sales and shrinking margins, the market values Tesla in the low-to-middle part of its own 5-year price-to-sales range, not near the 399.81 top.

bull: The balance sheet is strong: 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity, so there is no funding risk.
Trailing revenue still grew to 103.6B from 95.6B, and analysts expect next-year EPS growth of 25%.
Options traders hold the most open contracts in the 400 call (15193), and the put/call open-interest ratio is 0.77, so positioning leans toward upside.
bear: Latest-quarter sales fell 0.17% from a year earlier, and operating margin dropped to 3.35% from 4.74%.
Trailing free cash flow halved to 3.3B from 6.8B, while inventory rose 15% against flat sales.
The price is 423.3 times earnings and above every DCF value (base 24.66, bull 44.3). The business is graded D, and the committee call is Reduce.

levels.what: Today's close. It is near the own-history top of 399.81 and far above the DCF base of 24.66, so there is no value support here.
Bottom of the nearest support zone (363.93–368.69), where buyers have stepped in 4 times. A close below it would end the rebound and point toward 349.31–354.07.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine here only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74%.

longterm.why: Margins, cash flow and returns on investment are all falling, and the price sits near the top of its own valuation history. The merger report adds governance uncertainty but no business improvement.

swing.why: The price sits between support at 363.93–368.69 and resistance at 393.63–404.4 (touched 5 times), the trend is marked as down, and all three averages are flat, so there is no clean setup. No trade until a close above 404.4, or a pullback that holds 363.93–368.69.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report. Options price a 10.7% move by 2026-12-18 and a 19.0% move by 2027-02-19, which covers the report. Recent actual swings (72.9) have been larger than what options imply (51.5), and any filed merger terms could move the price before earnings.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth back toward the 15.78% of two quarters ago. That would make me reconsider, starting near 293.94.
A daily close above 404.4, the top of the resistance zone touched 5 times, would break the range and allow a swing entry.
A filed merger agreement whose terms are published. That would turn the report into a confirmed event, and the valuation would need to be redone on those terms.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid; the price held at 384.68 inside the 380.15–389.95 zone and under resistance at 393.63–404.4, and the reported SpaceX merger talk added no change to the shrinking margins or cash flow.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
